tip: Making the final video file from your project.
meaning: Exporting builds every frame and sound of the project and saves them as a normal video file you can share. Your project stays unchanged.
example: After editing, you press export and get birthday.mp4.
vukem: An export is a job: it renders the current revision, encodes the file and checks it. See [Exporting](/docs/guide/exporting).

tip: A finished file you hand to someone, made in the format they asked for.
meaning: Different places want different files: one for the web, one for TV, one with captions. Each of them is a deliverable.
example: A square video for a social post and a wide video for a website.

tip: The best-quality finished version, from which the other copies are made.
meaning: A master is exported at high quality once. Smaller copies for the web or phones are made from it, so you do not have to edit again.
example: You keep the big master and make a small version for messages.

tip: The app or website where the video will be watched, like YouTube or TikTok.
meaning: Each platform prefers a shape, a size and a length, and it recompresses your video. Knowing the platform helps to choose the settings.
example: A vertical video for TikTok and a wide one for YouTube.

tip: Videos that last up to a minute or so, made for phones.
meaning: Short-form videos are quick, vertical and usually have captions. Examples are Reels, Shorts and TikToks.
example: A 20-second recipe.
vukem: Vukem Video starts with 9:16 and word-timed captions for this use.

tip: The first seconds of a video, made to make people keep watching.
meaning: On a feed people decide in a moment. A hook is a question, a surprise or a strong picture right at the start.
example: "You are peeling bananas wrong" in the first second.

tip: A line that asks the viewer to do something, like "subscribe".
meaning: A call to action (CTA) tells viewers what to do next: visit, buy, follow, share.
example: "Follow for more tips" at the end of a video.

tip: The short opening and the closing parts of a video.
meaning: An intro (opening) says what the video is or who made it. An outro (ending) wraps it up, often with thanks and a call to action.
example: A channel logo animation at the start and a "thank you" card at the end.

tip: A very short video that makes people curious about something coming.
meaning: A teaser shows just a little of a product or a story to get attention before the main release.
example: A 15-second preview of a new game.

tip: A short preview of a longer film or show.
meaning: A trailer shows the best moments of a movie to make people want to watch it.
example: The two-minute video before a film comes out.

tip: A short video made to sell something.
meaning: A commercial (or ad) shows a product, says why it is good and ends with how to get it.
example: A 30-second advert for a toy.
vukem: Product commercials are one of the two use cases Vukem Video is built for.

tip: The small picture that represents a video in a list.
meaning: A thumbnail is the cover of a video. A clear, bright one makes more people press play.
example: The picture you see before you click a video.

tip: The single frame shown before the video starts.
meaning: A poster frame is the picture a player shows until you press play. It can be any frame of the video or a separate image.
example: A still of the main character shown on a web page.
vukem: `--format png --at 2s` exports a frame to use as a poster.

tip: A faint logo or name placed on a video to show who owns it.
meaning: A watermark is a small semi-transparent mark, often in a corner. It helps to say who made the video.
example: A channel logo in the lower right corner.

tip: Compressing a video again, which can lower its quality a bit.
meaning: Every time lossy video is saved again, a bit of quality is lost. Many sites re-encode what you upload, so give them a good source.
example: A video uploaded to a platform looks a little softer than your original.

tip: A small, light copy of a video used to edit smoothly.
meaning: Big 4K videos can be slow to play while you edit. A proxy is a small stand-in that is easy to play. The final export still uses the original.
example: Editing with low-resolution copies and exporting with the full ones.
vukem: The preview plays a proxy that ingest writes for each video. See [Media library](/docs/guide/media-library).

tip: Watching a video while it downloads, without saving the whole file first.
meaning: A streaming site sends small pieces of video just before you need them. It may lower the quality if your connection is slow.
example: Watching a film that begins at once.

tip: The site changes video quality while you watch, depending on your connection.
meaning: The video is stored in several qualities, and the player switches between them as the internet speed changes.
example: A video becomes blurry for a moment when you walk away from the Wi-Fi.

tip: Showing a video from one site inside a page of another site.
meaning: Embedding puts a video player into a web page, while the file stays on the first site.
example: A YouTube player inside a blog post.

tip: A video that starts by itself, usually without sound.
meaning: On feeds, videos play by themselves and muted. That is why captions matter: most people watch before they turn the sound on.
example: A video in the feed that starts silently as you scroll.

tip: A saved group of export settings, so you do not set them again.
meaning: A preset remembers the format, size and quality for a purpose, like "web" or "social".
example: One click to export with the same settings as last time.

tip: A task the computer does in the background, with a progress you can watch.
meaning: Exporting can take a while. It runs as a job, so you can keep working and check how it is going.
example: A progress bar filling while you do something else.
vukem: Exports and transcriptions are jobs. See [Jobs](/docs/guide/jobs).

tip: An automatic check that finds mistakes before you export.
meaning: A linter reads your project and warns about problems: text outside the safe area, an empty gap, a clip missing its media.
example: A warning that a caption is too close to the edge.
vukem: `vukem-video lint` and the `lint` tool. An export is refused while the lint finds an error.

tip: Checking that the exported file is really good before saying it is done.
meaning: After exporting, a program can open the file and check that it has video and sound, the right length and size.
example: Opening a freshly baked cake to make sure it is cooked.
vukem: An MP4 export reports success only after both streams and the duration are checked.

tip: An extra copy of your work, kept in another place.
meaning: Files can be lost. A backup lets you recover. Keep your originals and your project copied in two places.
example: Saving your project to an external drive as well.

tip: One file that holds a project with all it needs, to move or share it.
meaning: A bundle packs the project, its media and fonts together, so someone else can open it on another computer.
example: Sending the whole project to a friend in one file.

tip: The biggest picture size a platform or tool accepts.
meaning: Apps limit the size and length of a video. Larger ones are refused or shrunk.
example: A short video app that only takes up to 1080 by 1920.
vukem: Vukem Video accepts frames up to 4096 pixels on a side.

tip: Showing a draft to others and collecting their opinions.
meaning: A review is when people watch an unfinished video and say what to change, before the final one.
example: Your teacher watches the draft and asks to shorten the intro.

tip: One saved state of a video, like v1, v2 and v3.
meaning: Keeping versions lets you go back to an earlier idea if the new one is worse.
example: "teaser_v3.mp4" is the third try.
vukem: Every change raises the project's revision, so you can undo.
